label: The Tits Metric and Visibility
notes: Welcome to II.9, spanning printed pages 277 through 298. We have a boundary at infinity as a set; now we metrize it. Two metrics appear: the angular metric, read off from interior angles, and the Tits metric, its associated length metric. The payoff is that this geometry detects flats and distinguishes negative curvature from higher rank.

label: From Set to Metric Boundary
notes: Recall the boundary is asymptote classes of geodesic rays. As a set it is only a topological sphere. The plan is to enrich it: define an angle between ideal points, check it is a metric, then pass to its induced length metric. Each step is grounded in interior Alexandrov angles, so the curvature bound transfers to the boundary.

label: The Angular Metric
notes: Fix a basepoint and shoot the two rays toward distinct ideal points; their Alexandrov angle at that basepoint is one estimate of separation. The angular metric takes the supremum over all basepoints. In a CAT(0) space the angle does not decrease as you move the vertex outward, so this supremum is realized in the limit and is genuinely a metric.

label: Angle Stabilizes at Infinity
notes: Walk the observation point along a ray and watch the subtended angle between two fixed ideal points. By convexity of the metric the angle is monotone and converges. That stable limit is the Tits angle. The picture to hold is a shrinking or settling wedge whose opening reaches a definite asymptotic value, independent of how you traveled out.

label: The Tits Metric
notes: The angular metric can be disconnected or have short cuts that no path realizes, so we take its associated length metric. The Tits distance is the infimum of angular lengths of paths joining two ideal points, capped appropriately. This length metric is the Tits metric, and the boundary equipped with it is the Tits boundary of the space.

label: The Boundary is CAT(1)
notes: Here is the central theorem. If X is a complete CAT(0) space, its Tits boundary is a complete CAT(1) space. Comparison triangles in the boundary are read in the unit sphere. This is why angles capped at pi matter: the boundary inherits curvature bounded above by one, the natural scale for a sphere of ideal directions.

label: Flats Become Round Spheres
notes: Take a flat, an isometrically embedded Euclidean n-space. Its ideal directions form a round (n minus one)-sphere, and inside the Tits boundary that sphere appears with its standard metric of diameter pi. So a Euclidean plane contributes a great circle of circumference two pi. The Tits boundary literally photographs every flat as a round subsphere.

label: Visibility Spaces
notes: A CAT(0) space is a visibility space when any two distinct ideal points are joined by a geodesic line running between them. Equivalently the Tits distance between any two distinct boundary points is infinite, more than pi. Visibility is the boundary-level signature of genuinely negative curvature: every pair of ends sees one another along a bi-infinite geodesic.

label: Hyperbolic Space is Visibility
notes: Real hyperbolic n-space is the model visibility space. Any two distinct points on its sphere at infinity are the two ends of a unique geodesic line. In the Tits metric the boundary is totally disconnected with all distances infinite, since no flat strip exists to interpolate angles. Strict negativity forbids the rays from running parallel.

label: Flats versus Visibility
notes: Contrast the two regimes side by side. In a flat, parallel rays give Tits distance pi and the boundary is a round sphere with finite diameter. In a visibility space, divergence is exponential, Tits distance is infinite, and the boundary carries the discrete metric. Mixed spaces have flats inside an otherwise visibility-like geometry, breaking pure visibility.

label: Detecting Rank and Splittings
notes: The Tits boundary is a rank detector. A spherical join in the Tits boundary signals a product splitting of the space; an embedded round sphere of dimension at least one signals a higher-rank flat. This circle of ideas feeds rank rigidity: controlling Tits-boundary spheres constrains how the space can decompose into Euclidean and irreducible factors.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: To recap pages 277 through 298: the angular metric is the supremum of interior angles, the Tits metric is its length metric, and the Tits boundary of a CAT(0) space is CAT(1). Flats appear as round spheres of diameter pi, visibility spaces have infinite Tits distances, and these invariants drive splitting and rank-rigidity arguments.
